name: fleet100_r03
prompt:
One image: a sprite sheet of 9 cars for a 2D top-down city game.

THE VIEW MUST BE EXACTLY OVERHEAD. These cars were drawn before as if seen a little from one side: the lower flank's doors, door handles and side windows showed along the bottom edge, and the roof sat above the middle of the body. Draw each one from directly above the middle of its roof, like a plan drawing: the roof centred across the body's width, and neither flank seen more than the other. Worn paint and rust may differ side to side; the view may not.

Style: match the attached picture's art style exactly — outline weight, shading, highlights, level of detail, pixel size.

View: straight down from directly above the middle of each roof, orthographic, as the attached cars are: the roof centred across the body, and neither flank seen more than the other — no doors, sills or side windows showing along one side. No perspective, no ground, no shadow.

Layout: a 3×3 grid, the cars in the order listed, left to right and top to bottom. Each car lies horizontally with its nose to the right, centred in its place, with empty space round it. One shared scale for all.

Every car:
- Its length and width as listed, in that proportion, with straight flanks. Narrow cars stay narrow: leave spare room empty rather than draw a car wider.
- Its shape mirror-symmetric about its long centre line, with two small side mirrors just ahead of the windscreen; wear, rust and odd panels may differ side to side.
- Roof on. No tyres or wheels (the game draws them), no people, no text, logos, badges or licence plates.

Background: fully transparent outside the cars — no colour, no glow or halo, no shadow. Each car's edge ends sharply.

The cars in the picture only show the style: draw the cars listed, in their own colours. They are drawn at one scale, as the sheet's cars are: a longer car there is a longer drawing.
- Lamps switched off (unlit glass, no glow). Front corner: a headlamp and, beside it, a separate amber indicator. Rear corner: three separate small lenses side by side, each in its own thin dark frame, as distinct as the front's — red tail and brake lamp outermost, amber indicator next, white reversing lamp innermost. The rear indicator is the same amber as the front one and as large, plainly not red. Never one merged red cluster, never a light bar across the car.
- Condition shows only in the paint (faded colour, rust spots, a panel in another shade); the body outline is whole.

Cars, body length × width without mirrors, and what each is:
1. 4.01 × 1.65 m (2.43× longer than wide), nearly square corners — late-1980s Soviet wedge five-door hatchback, average condition, silver, low sloping wedge bonnet, angular cabin, short upright hatch, black plastic bumpers, slim rectangular headlamps, wide flat tail lamps split into red, amber and white sections
2. 4.02 × 1.70 m (2.36× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — 1990s German three-door compact hatchback, worn: faded red paint, rust spots on the wheel arches, one door slightly darker red, level bonnet, long roof, upright hatch with wide pillars, round-cornered headlamps, tall tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens
3. 4.07 × 1.73 m (2.35× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — modern budget five-door hatchback, good condition, bright orange, rounded bonnet, tall roof with roof rails, upright hatch, black unpainted bumpers, tall headlamps, vertical tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens
4. 4.13 × 1.62 m (2.55× longer than wide), nearly square corners — 1980s Soviet four-door saloon, average condition, faded beige, completely boxy with flat panels and sharp square corners, long and slim, long flat bonnet, upright three-box roof, separate flat boot, thin chrome bumpers, square headlamps, wide flat tail lamps across the corners split into red, amber and white sections
5. 4.14 × 1.72 m (2.41× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — 2000s small leisure van, worn: faded red paint, scuffed black bumpers, short sloping bonnet, tall boxy body with a flat high roof, big square tailgate, roof bars, tall headlamps, tall narrow tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens
6. 4.24 × 1.68 m (2.52× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — 2000s budget compact four-door saloon, worn: faded dark green paint, rust spots on the wheel arches, one rear door in a lighter green, rounded bonnet, rounded roof, short separate boot, oval headlamps, round-cornered tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens
7. 4.28 × 1.69 m (2.53× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — 1990s compact estate car, worn: faded red paint, rust spots on the sills, one rear door in a slightly different red, rounded bonnet, long roof with roof rails to an upright tailgate, slim rectangular headlamps, tall tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens
8. 4.36 × 1.94 m (2.25× longer than wide), rounded corners — Soviet forward-control 4×4 minibus, worn: faded grey paint with rust at the corners. It has NO BONNET AND NO NOSE: seen from above, its front end is blunt — the body's front edge runs straight across with rounded corners, and the windscreen starts right at that edge. Behind it one long smooth domed roof, curving down to every edge like a loaf of bread, with no ribs, rails or panels. Its two headlamps are small and round, one at each front corner on the flat front face — not angled, not swept back. Small tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens
9. 4.41 × 1.79 m (2.46× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — modern small panel van, average condition, white with scuffs on the black bumpers, short sloping bonnet, tall flat roof, two square rear doors, large headlamps, tall tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens
